New shared wrapper (run_trusted_command/popen_trusted_command) introduced to structurally shrink this ratchet: every reviewed B603 call site so far (four reviews above) already used a fixed/validated argv yet still reproduced B603 the moment its nosec was removed -- Bandit flags any non-literal subprocess argv regardless of how safely it was constructed, so per-call-site nosecs were never going to collapse toward the 2027-04-30/20 and 2027-07-31/0 targets through individual review alone. This module centralizes the audited subprocess.run/Popen call to exactly two lines (one nosec each; kept, unavoidable for the same reason as the other reviews) so every caller carries zero nosec of its own. Phase 1 migrated 8 low-risk call sites to it: scripts/ci/check_ruff_debt_baseline.py, scripts/doctor_production_readiness.py, scripts/sync_postgres_password.py, launcher/process.py, core/doctor/__init__.py (x2), core/multimodal.py (x2), main.py (x3) -- 13 individual suppressions removed, 2 added here, net -11 (verified via bandit -r . before/after each migration). tools/audit_imports.py was deliberately left unmigrated: it has no sys.path setup and no established precedent of importing from core/, so its invocation context (bare `python tools/audit_imports.py`) is not guaranteed to have the repo root on sys.path -- the risk of breaking a standalone dev tool for one suppression wasn't worth it. 100% covered by tests/unit/core/test_trusted_subprocess.py (shell=True rejection, empty-command rejection, embedded-NUL rejection, and the happy path for both run and Popen). Full-repo Bandit skipped_tests dropped 39 -> 30 in this phase; maximum_skipped_tests ratcheted down in the same commit per policy. Remaining B603 sites (managers/code/*, web/plugins/sandbox.py, web/process_lifecycle.py, managers/system_health.py, tools/audit_imports.py) are planned for later phases of the same migration, in ascending order of risk.

Full-repo Bandit skipped_tests dropped 30 -> 23; maximum_skipped_tests ratcheted down in the same commit per policy. Remaining B603/B102 sites (web/plugins/sandbox.py, managers/code/docker_lifecycle.py, tools/audit_imports.py) are Phase 3, planned as a separate PR given the higher stakes.

New shared wrapper (urlopen_trusted_request()), the same centralizing pattern as trusted_subprocess.py but for B310 (urllib_urlopen) instead of B603 -- Bandit flags any urlopen call regardless of URL construction since it can't statically prove the scheme excludes file://ftp://etc. Every current B310 call site already targets a fixed https:// origin. Migrated 2 call sites: github_upload.py's open_upload_pull_request() helper and scripts/install_modules/refresh_remote_checksums.py's fetch_remote_bytes() (net -2, verified via tests/unit/root/test_github_upload.py's existing gu.urllib.request.urlopen mocks -- same shared-module-attribute mechanism proven throughout this migration -- and tests/unit/scripts/test_refresh_remote_checksums.py). 100% covered by tests/unit/core/test_trusted_urlopen.py (scheme rejection before any urlopen call, happy-path forwarding -- mocked, not a real socket, per this repo's unit-test network guard in tests/unit/conftest.py). scripts/ci/check_gpu_runner_capacity.py and scripts/ci/check_benchmark_runner_capacity.py's B310 sites were deliberately NOT migrated -- see their own review entries below; both are architecturally different from refresh_remote_checksums.py (whose workflow does run uv sync) in a way that matters here.

Both B310 sites already target a fixed https://api.github.com origin with a caller-supplied repository path (not otherwise attacker-controlled) -- same unavoidable-Bandit-suspicion class as every other reviewed call site. Deliberately NOT migrated to core/utils/trusted_urlopen.py despite that wrapper now existing, unlike every other file in this ratchet reduction: both scripts' real production workflows (.github/workflows/gpu-runner-capacity-watchdog.yml, benchmark-runner-capacity-watchdog.yml) run them as bare `python scripts/ci/check_*.py` with only actions/checkout + actions/setup-python -- no astral-sh/setup-uv, no `uv sync`, the project's own dependencies (including core/) are never installed. Both scripts are intentionally dependency-free (stdlib-only imports: argparse/json/os/sys/urllib), a deliberate architectural choice for a bare, unattended, hourly-scheduled capacity monitor. Verified empirically that a direct `python <script>` invocation cannot resolve `import core` (the script's own directory lands on sys.path[0], not the repo root, and there is no installed package to fall back on) -- the same failure mode already fixed properly (with a sys.path bootstrap) for tools/audit_imports.py, but here the deeper problem is that core/ has never been installed at all in this execution context, which a sys.path bootstrap alone cannot fix. Making these two scripts depend on core/ would create a standing invariant (every module core/__init__.py transitively imports at module level must forever stay lazy/stdlib-only) that nothing in CI currently tests for, silently breaking an unattended production monitor the moment that invariant is violated -- not worth 2 suppressions. No safe reduction found without either accepting that risk or duplicating a local, unshared urlopen wrapper in each file (which would not reduce Bandit's count at all -- the suppression still has to live somewhere Bandit can see it).
